claims.title: Cattle-herding cultures in the Sudd
claims.summary: Archaeological evidence indicates transhumant cattle-raising societies established in the Sudd marshlands of the upper White Nile.

sources.label: Precolonial History of South Sudan
sources.publisher: Oxford Research Encyclopedia of African History

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-3000bce-cattle-herding-cultures-in-the-sudd, claim TL:SDS:event:3000bce:cattle-herding-cultures-in-the-sudd, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nilotic expansion across the upper Nile
claims.summary: Western Nilotic peoples including the Dinka and Nuer spread out from the Sudd, a dispersal linked to the decline of the Christian Nubian kingdoms of Makuria and Alodia.

sources.label: Precolonial History of South Sudan
sources.publisher: Oxford Research Encyclopedia of African History

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1400-nilotic-expansion-across-the-upper-nile, claim TL:SDS:event:1400:nilotic-expansion-across-the-upper-nile, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Shilluk Kingdom
claims.summary: The Shilluk establish a centralised kingdom on the White Nile under the sacred kingship of the Reth, traditionally traced to the founder-figure Nyikang.

sources.label: Precolonial History of South Sudan
sources.publisher: Oxford Research Encyclopedia of African History

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1450-founding-of-the-shilluk-kingdom, claim TL:SDS:event:1450:founding-of-the-shilluk-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fashoda made the Shilluk royal seat
claims.summary: King Tugo founds Fashoda as the permanent residence of the Shilluk kings, formalising the kingdom's investiture rituals and divine kingship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1690-fashoda-made-the-shilluk-royal-seat, claim TL:SDS:event:1690:fashoda-made-the-shilluk-royal-seat, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Turco-Egyptian conquest reaches Sudan
claims.summary: Muhammad Ali's forces conquer the Funj lands and extend Egyptian rule up the Nile, seeking gold, ivory and slaves and making Khartoum the seat of administration.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1821-turco-egyptian-conquest-reaches-sudan, claim TL:SDS:event:1821:turco-egyptian-conquest-reaches-sudan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zariba slave and ivory raids
claims.summary: Armed traders such as al-Zubayr Rahma Mansur establish fortified zaribas across the south; contemporary estimates put captives taken at tens of thousands a year by the mid-1870s.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1860-zariba-slave-and-ivory-raids, claim TL:SDS:event:1860:zariba-slave-and-ivory-raids, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Equatoria province established
claims.summary: Samuel Baker is appointed governor of Equatoria, an Egyptian southern province later led by Charles Gordon, partly to suppress the slave trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1869-equatoria-province-established, claim TL:SDS:event:1869:equatoria-province-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mahdist revolt and the fall of Khartoum
claims.summary: The Mahdist uprising overruns Sudan and captures Khartoum, ending Turco-Egyptian rule and bringing further upheaval to the southern Nile peoples.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1885-mahdist-revolt-and-the-fall-of-khartoum, claim TL:SDS:event:1885:mahdist-revolt-and-the-fall-of-khartoum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mahdist state crushed at Omdurman
claims.summary: An Anglo-Egyptian army defeats the Mahdist forces at Omdurman, clearing the way for the reconquest of Sudan, including the south.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1898-mahdist-state-crushed-at-omdurman, claim TL:SDS:event:1898:mahdist-state-crushed-at-omdurman, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Anglo-Egyptian Condominium established
claims.summary: Britain and Egypt establish joint rule over Sudan, with the largely Christian and traditionalist south administered separately from the Arab-Muslim north.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1899-anglo-egyptian-condominium-established, claim TL:SDS:event:1899:anglo-egyptian-condominium-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Closed District ordinances
claims.summary: Colonial 'closed district' rules restrict travel and trade between north and south, isolating the southern provinces and curbing northern and Arabic influence.

sources.label: British policy in Anglo-Egyptian Sudan and the north–south divide
sources.publisher: Africa at LSE, London School of Economics

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1922-closed-district-ordinances, claim TL:SDS:event:1922:closed-district-ordinances, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Southern Policy formalised
claims.summary: A government memorandum directs administrators to develop the south as a distinct bloc, favouring local languages and English over Arabic and limiting northern contact.

sources.label: British policy in Anglo-Egyptian Sudan and the north–south divide
sources.publisher: Africa at LSE, London School of Economics

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1930-the-southern-policy-formalised, claim TL:SDS:event:1930:the-southern-policy-formalised, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Britain reverses course
claims.summary: Colonial authorities abandon the Southern Policy and move to unite the south with the north, without meaningful consultation of southerners.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1946-britain-reverses-course, claim TL:SDS:event:1946:britain-reverses-course, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Juba Conference
claims.summary: Northern and southern representatives meet at Juba to discuss the south's place in a future Sudan, but southern delegates have little leverage over the outcome.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1947-juba-conference, claim TL:SDS:event:1947:juba-conference, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Torit mutiny begins the First Civil War
claims.summary: Southern soldiers of the Equatorial Corps mutiny at Torit over fears of northern domination, an event marking the start of the First Sudanese Civil War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1955-torit-mutiny-begins-the-first-civil-war, claim TL:SDS:event:1955:torit-mutiny-begins-the-first-civil-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sudan's independence; the south sidelined
claims.summary: Sudan becomes independent under a northern-dominated government, with southern demands for federalism largely unmet.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1956-sudan-s-independence-the-south-sidelined, claim TL:SDS:event:1956:sudan-s-independence-the-south-sidelined, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Addis Ababa Agreement
claims.summary: The Addis Ababa Agreement ends the seventeen-year first war, granting the south a single autonomous region and integrating Anyanya fighters into Sudan's forces.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1972-addis-ababa-agreement, claim TL:SDS:event:1972:addis-ababa-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Second Civil War and the rise of the SPLM/SPLA
claims.summary: Khartoum abolishes southern autonomy and moves to impose sharia; the SPLM/SPLA forms under John Garang, beginning the Second Sudanese Civil War.

sources.label: South Sudan: The 2005 Comprehensive Peace Agreement, Conflict, Independence

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1983-second-civil-war-and-the-rise-of-the-splm-spla, claim TL:SDS:event:1983:second-civil-war-and-the-rise-of-the-splm-spla, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: An estimated two million dead
claims.summary: Over more than two decades the war kills around two million people through combat, famine and disease and uproots millions, among the deadliest conflicts of its time.

sources.label: South Sudan: The 2005 Comprehensive Peace Agreement, Conflict, Independence
Ten Years Later: Taking Stock of Sudan's Comprehensive Peace Agreement

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-1983-an-estimated-two-million-dead, claim TL:SDS:event:1983:an-estimated-two-million-dead, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Comprehensive Peace Agreement signed
claims.summary: Khartoum and the SPLM/SPLA sign the CPA, ending the second war and providing for southern autonomy and a self-determination referendum within six years.

sources.label: South Sudan: The 2005 Comprehensive Peace Agreement, Conflict, Independence
Ten Years Later: Taking Stock of Sudan's Comprehensive Peace Agreement

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-2005-comprehensive-peace-agreement-signed, claim TL:SDS:event:2005:comprehensive-peace-agreement-signed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of John Garang
claims.summary: Weeks after becoming Sudan's first vice-president, John Garang dies in a helicopter crash; Salva Kiir Mayardit succeeds him as SPLM leader and southern president.

sources.label: South Sudan: The 2005 Comprehensive Peace Agreement, Conflict, Independence
Ten Years Later: Taking Stock of Sudan's Comprehensive Peace Agreement

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-2005-death-of-john-garang, claim TL:SDS:event:2005:death-of-john-garang, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Self-determination referendum
claims.summary: In a week-long vote, 98.83% of southern Sudanese choose independence on a turnout of about 99%.

sources.label: Referendum in Southern Sudan
sources.publisher: United Nations Mission in the Sudan (UNMIS)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-2011-self-determination-referendum, claim TL:SDS:event:2011:self-determination-referendum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of South Sudan
claims.summary: At midnight on 9 July 2011 South Sudan becomes an independent state, the world's newest widely recognised nation, recognised the same day by the United States and others.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-2011-independence-of-south-sudan, claim TL:SDS:event:2011:independence-of-south-sudan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Admission to the United Nations
claims.summary: South Sudan is admitted as the 193rd member state of the United Nations, and soon after joins the African Union.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-2011-admission-to-the-united-nations, claim TL:SDS:event:2011:admission-to-the-united-nations, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Civil war erupts in Juba
claims.summary: A power struggle between President Salva Kiir and former vice-president Riek Machar ignites fighting in Juba that spreads nationwide and takes on an ethnic character.

sources.label: Civil war in South Sudan: a primer

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-2013-civil-war-erupts-in-juba, claim TL:SDS:event:2013:civil-war-erupts-in-juba, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Famine declared in Unity state
claims.summary: The UN declares famine in parts of Unity state, with millions needing emergency aid; experts warn that famine used as a weapon of war may be an international crime.

sources.label: Famine declared in region of South Sudan

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Sudan: From the cattle camps of the Nile to the world's newest nation", terralore.co/country/SDS/chronicle#ev-2017-famine-declared-in-unity-state, claim TL:SDS:event:2017:famine-declared-in-unity-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: An estimated 383,000 dead
claims.summary: A London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine study estimates about 383,000 conflict-related deaths by April 2018, roughly half from direct violence.

sources.label: Estimates of crisis-attributable mortality in South Sudan
sources.publisher: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine

claims.title: Revitalised peace agreement (R-ARCSS)
claims.summary: After repeated failed ceasefires, the government and opposition sign the R-ARCSS, providing for a unified army, a new constitution and elections.

sources.label: The Formation of the Revitalized Transitional Government of National Unity in South Sudan

claims.title: Unity government formed
claims.summary: A Revitalised Transitional Government of National Unity is sworn in, with Riek Machar again first vice-president under President Salva Kiir, though the peace remains fragile.

sources.label: The Formation of the Revitalized Transitional Government of National Unity in South Sudan
